T: A boy, a pelican and the Coorong.
D: A boy living with his reclusive dad on the wild South Australian coast raises an orphaned pelican called Mr Percival.
P: Serve the fish when Hideaway Tom brings in the catch.
S: Hollow-crusted damper with butter, golden syrup and lemon myrtle salt

Crusty bush damper with a soft inside, torn warm and served with butter, golden syrup and a little dish of lemon myrtle salt. Rub 60g cold butter into 450g self-raising flour and 1 tsp salt until it looks like breadcrumbs. Stir in 300ml milk to make a soft dough and knead briefly. Shape into a round, cut a cross in the top and dust with flour. Bake at 200C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow when tapped. Mix 1 tsp sea salt with 1/2 tsp ground lemon myrtle. Serve warm with butter, golden syrup and the salt.
Pipis steamed open in garlic, chilli, lemon butter, with crusty bread

Pipis steamed open with garlic, chilli and a splash of stock, finished with butter, lemon and parsley and served with crusty bread. Soak 1kg pipis in cold salted water for 1 hour to purge the sand, then rinse. Fry 3 sliced garlic cloves and 1 sliced red chilli in 2 tbsp olive oil for 1 minute. Add the pipis and 100ml fish stock, cover and steam 3 to 4 minutes until they open, discarding any that stay shut. Stir in 30g butter, the juice of 1 lemon and chopped parsley. Serve with crusty bread.
M: Hideaway Tom's crisp fish and chips
Battered white fish with chicken salt chips and homemade tartare

Crisp battered fish fillets with thick chips, lemon, tartare sauce and chicken salt, eaten out of paper like at the shack. Bake 1kg frozen thick-cut chips at 220C for 30 minutes. Whisk 150g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder and 250ml cold soda water into a batter. Dust 4 firm white fish fillets in flour, dip in the batter and fry at 180C for 5 minutes until golden. Mix 150g mayonnaise with chopped capers, pickles and dill for tartare. Toss the chips in chicken salt and serve wrapped in paper with lemon.
W: Soft dumplings poached in hot golden syrup sauce

Soft fluffy dumplings simmered in a buttery golden syrup sauce until sticky, served with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Rub 50g butter into 200g self-raising flour, then stir in 1 egg and 80ml milk to a soft dough. In a wide pan, bring 250ml water, 125ml golden syrup, 80g brown sugar and 30g butter to the boil. Drop in tablespoons of dough, cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes without lifting the lid. Spoon into bowls with the sauce and serve with vanilla ice cream.
K: Strong black tea with lemon myrtle and honey, brewed in a billy

Black tea brewed strong in a billy with lemon myrtle and a gum leaf, sweetened with honey and served with milk on the side. Bring 1.2L water to the boil in a billy or saucepan. Add 6 black tea bags, 1 tsp dried lemon myrtle and 1 clean gum leaf if you have one, and take off the heat. Steep 5 minutes, then remove the bags and leaf. Stir in 2 tbsp honey. Pour into 4 enamel mugs and serve with milk on the side.
